answer.location_description: A horizontal band along the top edge of the image (rows 0-3), spanning most of the width and strongest over the left and central columns. This is far from the centred nodule.
answer.shortcut_type: bright band/marker at top image border
answer.mechanism: Layer-1 unit 23 (bias +26) has large positive weights concentrated almost entirely in rows 0-3 and near-random weights elsewhere, so it acts as a detector for brightness in the top strip. In layer 2 it feeds strongly into u1 (+76, output -79), u8 (+92, output -43), u3 (-80, output +53) and u14 (-80, output +91). This lowers the malignancy logit through these pathways, only partly offset by u15/u6/u5. Assuming all layer-2 units are active, its linearised net contribution is about -6000 integer units, so it pushes toward benign. Because the sign depends on which layer-2 units are active, the direction is less certain than the location.
answer.evidence: In unit 23, rows r0-r3 are dominated by large positive integers (r0: 56,80,86,79,68,63,80,89,53,71; r1: 84,65,68,65,64,62,85,80,84; r2: 63,73,54,54,63,66,70,78,65; r3: 87,69,70,74,70,68,75,73,81,81). Several exceed the roughly ±80 range of the untrained-looking units. Rows 4-20 of the same unit look like noise. No other unit has such a sharp edge-localised pattern. The nodule-detecting units have centre-localised positive weights: unit 1, unit 8 (rows 5-21, cols 4-18), unit 18 (rows 9-19 centre), unit 20 (rows 6-18, cols 6-16) and unit 29 (rows 6-19, cols 5-17). Linearised through layers 2-3, units 1, 8, 18 and 20 give clearly positive (malignant) contributions, while unit 23 gives a net negative one.
answer.main_feature: The genuine signal is the amount and extent of bright (dense) tissue in the central region, i.e. nodule size/solidity, detected by centre-weighted units 1, 8, 18, 20 and 29; more central density pushes toward malignant. Unit 17 adds a centre-versus-surround contrast.
